opening_message:
Ticket 1: Erika Bolton (employee ID E002) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E002.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Erika Bolton (E002) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin to Payroll. Admin requires role ownership of the system (Payroll Specialist); as an Analyst, maximum is write. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Erika Bolton (E002) is a contractor with basic security training (Security DB), requesting admin to Payroll. Contractors can never have admin; with basic training the maximum is read. Recommend read. (Note: earlier note listed her as full-time, but Security DB shows contractor — basing recommendation on Security DB.)
reason: Erika Bolton (E002) requested admin access to Payroll. Admin can never be granted to contractors, and per the Security agent's verified database lookup, E002 is a contractor with basic security training, so the maximum allowed level is read (HR's conflicting full_time note is contradicted by Security DB, which the Security agent explicitly used as the basis). Since admin exceeds the maximum of read, grant the maximum: read.
